Every day can be run as written, and it fits her five-day schedule.

── MARISOL'S WEEK ──
Marisol is training for a second marathon, the Wexley Lakes Marathon, aiming to break 3:45 after a 4:02 debut. Marisol runs five days a week, with a session on Wednesday, the long run on Sunday and Monday and Friday off, and ran about 30 miles a week before this build.
Recent weeks: 53, 40, 42, 46 mi
This week: 34 mi over 5 runs.
Body: "Legs heavy and flat. Nothing hurts, they just feel dead."
Feeling: "Nervous. I feel like I'm losing fitness."
Asks: "Is it crazy to do one more 16-miler on Wednesday so I feel ready?"

── THE DRAFT ──
Tells Marisol: Skip the extra 16-miler: your fitness is built, and heavy legs this week are what a taper feels like. …
Answers: (1) Yes, it would hurt more than it helps, so leave it out. A long run four days before a marathon takes about a week to recover from, and you would start the race still carrying it. (2) Your 20-milers on Sun Sep 13 and Sun Oct 4 already built the endurance, and one more run cannot add to it in time.
